children: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd (NSE:TMPV) reported a Q2 FY27 net loss of Rs. 5,531 crore, including Rs. 6,738 crore in exceptional charges, while revenue rose 34% to Rs. 96,920 crore. JLR cut its FY27 adjusted operating margin forecast to 2–3% from 4% and its revenue outlook to about £25 billion from £26 billion.
: TMPV posted a Q2 FY27 net loss of Rs. 5,531 crore, including Rs. 6,738 crore in exceptional charges. Revenue rose 34% to Rs. 96,920 crore; EBITDA margin improved 630 bps to 6.2%.
: TMPV’s JLR cut its FY27 adjusted operating margin forecast to 2–3% from 4% and revenue outlook to about £25 billion from £26 billion. It expects £1.25 billion net cash outflow.
: Motilal Oswal kept its Sell rating on TMPV with a Rs. 240 target, citing weak JLR demand, cost pressures and domestic margin risks. It cut FY27 EPS estimates 69% and FY28 estimates 5%.
: Nuvama kept its Buy rating on Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles but cut its target price to Rs. 360 from Rs. 450, citing expected growth in India and JLR, higher volumes and cost savings.
: TMPV signed an MoU giving Stellantis access to its product technology and vehicle architecture for global models. October 2026 sales hit a monthly record of 75,400 units.
: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles launched the Aeris and Osprey in South Africa, unveiled Curvv Series X and Sierra special editions, and expanded Battery-as-a-Service across its EV range.
: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd (TMPV) began its Q2 2027 earnings call.
